ko_meaning: 밥과 같이 먹는 여러 가지 음식
ko_meaning_en: The various foods you eat together with rice

example.en: This restaurant has lots of side dishes, so I like it.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'so' after 많다.
form.why: The stem 많 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 많아서. -어서 is for other vowels.

ko_meaning: 고기나 채소를 넣고 끓인, 국보다 물이 적은 음식
ko_meaning_en: A dish of meat or vegetables boiled with less water than soup

example.en: The kimchi stew my grandma made is the most delicious.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel
past noun modifier: 끓이 + ㄴ → 끓인

form.q_en: Pick the modifier for 'that grandma made'.
form.why: After a vowel stem the past modifier is just -ㄴ: 끓이 + ㄴ → 끓인. 끓은 would come from 끓다 'to boil (by itself)'.

ko_meaning: 고기를 달고 짜게 만들어서 구운 한국 음식
ko_meaning_en: A Korean dish of meat made sweet and salty and then grilled

example.en: Bulgogi is sweet, so even children eat it well.

tokens.note: 는 marks the topic after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 달다 + -아서/어서 ('sweet, so').
form.why: 달 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 달아서. ㄹ only drops before ㄴ, ㅂ or ㅅ, not here.

ko_meaning: 밥에 여러 가지 채소와 고추장을 넣고 섞어 먹는 음식
ko_meaning_en: Rice eaten mixed with various vegetables and red pepper paste

example.en: Bibimbap is spicy but delicious.

tokens.note: 은 marks the topic after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 비빔밥.
form.why: 비빔밥 ends in a consonant (ㅂ), so the topic particle is 은. 는 follows a vowel, and 을/에 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: A Korean food made from rice

example.en: I bought rice cakes at the market and ate them.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens
을 marks the object after a consonant
-아서 links two actions: 사 + 아서 → 사서

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 사다 + -아서 ('bought and then').
form.why: 사 + 아서 → 사서 (the two ㅏ merge). -아서 never takes the past tense, so 샀어서 is wrong.

ko_meaning: 고추처럼 입 안이 뜨겁고 아픈 맛이 나다
ko_meaning_en: To have a hot, stinging taste like chili pepper

example.en: The kimchi was spicy, so I drank water.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 맵다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: 맵다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 맵 + 어서 → 매워서.

ko_meaning_en: To taste strongly of salt

example.ko: 찌개가 너무 짜서 물을 더 넣었어요.
example.roman: Jjigaega neomu jjaseo mureul deo neoeosseoyo.
example.en: The stew was too salty, so I added more water.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 짜다 + -아서 ('salty, so').
form.why: 짜 + 아서 → 짜서 (the two ㅏ merge). -아서 never takes the past tense, so 짰어서 is wrong.

ko_meaning_en: To taste like sugar

example.en: I don't like sweet food.

tokens.note: 달 + ㄴ → 단 (ㄹ drops before ㄴ)

form.q_en: Pick the noun-modifier form of 달다 ('sweet food').
form.why: For a ㄹ-stem adjective, ㄹ drops and -ㄴ is added: 달 + ㄴ → 단.

ko_meaning_en: To taste like a lemon

example.en: If the juice is sour, add some sugar.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 시다 + -(으)면 ('if it is sour').
form.why: After a vowel stem, just add -면: 시 + 면 → 시면. -으면 is only for consonant stems.

ko_meaning_en: Food has little salt, so the taste is weak

example.en: Hospital food is bland, but it is good for your health.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 싱겁다 + -지만 ('bland, but').
form.why: -지만 attaches straight to the stem: 싱겁 + 지만. The ㅂ only changes before a vowel (싱거워요).

ko_meaning_en: White powder that makes food salty

example.en: I need to add a little more salt.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'have to' form of 넣다.
form.why: 넣 has ㅓ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어야: 넣어야 해요 = have to put in.

ko_meaning_en: White powder that gives a sweet taste

example.en: I don't put sugar in my coffee.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct ending for 'do not'.
form.why: -지 않다 means 'not'. 않다 is spelled with ㄶ and takes -아요: 않아요.

ko_meaning_en: The white grain before it is cooked into rice

example.en: I'm going to go to the supermarket to buy rice.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'to buy' (purpose of going).
form.why: -(으)러 shows the purpose of going. After a vowel stem add -러: 사 + 러 → 사러.

ko_meaning_en: A round vegetable that grows in the ground

example.en: Put in the potatoes and meat, then boil it.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 넣다 + -고 ('put in and then').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem with no extra vowel: 넣 + 고 → 넣고 (said [너코]).

ko_meaning_en: A round vegetable that makes you cry when you cut it

example.en: When I cut onions, tears come out.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 자르다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 자르 ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 자르면. The 르 change (잘라) only happens before -아/어.

ko_meaning_en: Tea made from green leaves

example.en: Green tea is good for the body, so I drink it every day.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 마시다.
form.why: 마시 + 어요 → 마셔요 (ㅣ + ㅓ join into ㅕ).

ko_meaning_en: An alcoholic drink with foam, made from barley

example.en: On hot days, a cold beer is great.

tokens.note: ㅂ irregular modifier: 덥 + 은 → 더운
에 marks time, 는 makes it the topic
가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 맥주.
form.why: 맥주 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 맥주, 소주, 와인 같은 마실 것
ko_meaning_en: Drinks such as beer, soju and wine

example.en: I have to drive, so I can't drink.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant
못 + verb = cannot; said [몬] before ㅁ

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'cannot'.
form.why: 못 before a verb means 'cannot'. 없, 아니 and 말 cannot negate a verb this way.

ko_meaning: 작고 빨간, 봄에 먹는 단 과일
ko_meaning_en: A small, red, sweet fruit eaten in spring

example.en: If strawberries are cheap, I'll buy a lot.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 사다.
form.why: After a vowel stem, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds just ㄹ: 사 + ㄹ → 살 거예요.

ko_meaning: 길고 노란 껍질이 있는 단 과일
ko_meaning_en: A sweet fruit with a long yellow peel

example.en: I ate two bananas in the morning.

tokens.note: 둘 becomes 두 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the right number before the counter 개.
form.why: Counters like 개 use native numbers, and 둘 becomes 두 before a counter. Sino-Korean 이 is not used with 개.

ko_meaning_en: To cook meat or bread over a fire or in heat

example.en: Yesterday I grilled meat with my family and we ate it.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 굽다 + -어서.
form.why: 굽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 굽 + 어서 → 구워서.

ko_meaning: 물이나 음식을 아주 뜨겁게 해서 거품이 나게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To heat water or food until it bubbles

example.en: I boiled some water and had coffee.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 끓이다 + -어서.
form.why: 끓이 + 어서 → 끓여서. 끓다 means 'to boil' by itself and cannot take 물을, and -어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: To cook food in oil while stirring it

example.en: Onions get sweet when you stir-fry them.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 볶다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 볶 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으면: 볶으면.

ko_meaning_en: To divide something with a knife or scissors

example.en: I got my hair cut at the hair salon.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 자르다.
form.why: 자르다 is 르-irregular: 자르 + 았어요 → 잘랐어요. 자랐어요 comes from 자라다 'to grow'.

ko_meaning_en: To make something go inside

example.ko: 오늘 비가 오니까 가방에 우산을 넣으세요.
example.roman: Oneul biga onikka gabang-e usaneul neoeuseyo.
example.en: It's raining today, so put an umbrella in your bag.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 넣다.
form.why: 넣 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으세요: 넣으세요.

ko_meaning: 식당에서 파는 음식의 이름과 값을 쓴 것
ko_meaning_en: A list of the names and prices of the food a restaurant sells

example.ko: 메뉴에 없는 음식은 시킬 수 없어요.
example.roman: Menyue eomneun eumsigeun sikil su eopseoyo.
example.en: You can't order food that isn't on the menu.

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 없다 ('that isn't there').
form.why: 있다 and 없다 take -는 when they describe a noun in the present: 없는 음식.

ko_meaning: 식당이나 가게에서 음식이나 물건을 달라고 하다
ko_meaning_en: To ask for food or goods at a restaurant or shop

example.en: I ordered the food and waited an hour.

tokens.note: 하나 becomes 한 before a counter

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'ordered and then'.
form.why: -고 links two actions in order and goes straight on the stem: 주문하고. -(으)러 needs 가다/오다 after it.

en: to order (food); to make someone do
ko_meaning: 음식을 가져다 달라고 하다; 다른 사람에게 일을 하게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To ask for food to be brought; to make someone else do a job

example.en: We ordered pizza and ate it at home.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 시키다 + -어서.
form.why: 시키 + 어서 → 시켜서 (ㅣ + ㅓ → ㅕ). -어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: To have eaten a lot so your stomach is full

example.en: I'm so full that I can't eat any more.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 배부르다 + -어서.
form.why: 배부르다 is 르-irregular: 르 + 어 becomes ㄹ러, so 배부르 + 어서 → 배불러서.

ko_meaning_en: To want to drink water

example.en: I exercised, so I'm thirsty.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 목마르다.
form.why: 목마르다 is 르-irregular. 마 has ㅏ, so 마르 + 아요 → 말라요: 목말라요.

ko_meaning_en: The place at home where you make food

example.en: My older brother is making ramen in the kitchen.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the place where an action happens.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action (cooking) happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: The place where you wash your hands or use the toilet

example.en: The bathroom was dirty, so I cleaned it.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 더럽다 + -어서.
form.why: 더럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 더럽 + 어서 → 더러워서.

ko_meaning: 가족이 같이 앉아서 쉬는 넓은 방
ko_meaning_en: The large room where the family sits and relaxes together

example.en: The living room is spacious and bright.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct spelling of 밝다 in the present.
form.why: 밝 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 밝아요. It sounds like [발가요] but is spelled 밝아요.

ko_meaning_en: A big machine that keeps food cold

example.en: There's beer in the fridge, so help yourself.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where something is (with 있다).
form.why: With 있다, use 에 for the place where something is. 에서 is for where an action happens.

ko_meaning_en: A machine that washes clothes

example.en: Laundry is easy because there's a washing machine.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 있다 + -(으)니까.
form.why: 있 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으니까: 있으니까.

ko_meaning: 여러 사람이 앉을 수 있는 크고 편한 의자
ko_meaning_en: A big, comfortable seat that several people can sit on

example.en: I sat on the sofa and read a book.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 앉다 + -아서.
form.why: 앉 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 앉아서 (said [안자서]).

ko_meaning_en: A machine you can watch broadcasts on

example.ko: 텔레비전을 너무 많이 보면 눈이 아파요.
example.roman: Tellebijeoneul neomu mani bomyeon nuni apayo.
example.en: If you watch too much TV, your eyes hurt.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 보다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 보 ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 보면.

ko_meaning_en: An object you look into to see your face or body

example.en: I looked in the mirror and put on my hat.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the verb used for putting on a hat.
form.why: Hats take 쓰다. 입다 is for clothes, 신다 for shoes and socks, and 매다 for ties.

ko_meaning_en: A large piece of furniture where you keep clothes

example.en: I put the winter clothes in the wardrobe.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you put something.
form.why: 넣다 takes 에 for the place things go into. 에서 marks where an action happens.

ko_meaning: 잘 때 몸 위에 덮는 크고 두꺼운 천
ko_meaning_en: A big, thick cloth you cover yourself with when you sleep

example.ko: 날씨가 추워서 이불을 하나 더 샀어요.
example.roman: Nalssiga chuwoseo ibureul hana deo sasseoyo.
example.en: It got cold, so I bought one more blanket.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'one' with no counter after it.
form.why: Without a counter, 'one' is 하나. 한 is used only right before a counter (한 개).

ko_meaning_en: To make a dirty place clean

example.en: Guests are coming, so I have to clean the room.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'have to clean'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to': 청소하 + 여야 → 청소해야 해요.

ko_meaning_en: To wash dirty clothes clean with water

example.en: If the weather is nice, I'll do the laundry.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 좋다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 좋 ends in a consonant, so it takes -으면: 좋으면 (said [조으면]).

ko_meaning_en: To make a light or a machine start working

example.en: It's dark, so turn on the light.

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite request form of 켜다.
form.why: 켜 ends in a vowel, so just add -세요: 켜세요.

ko_meaning_en: To make a light or a machine stop working

example.en: I turned off the TV and went to sleep.

form.q_en: Pick the past tense of 끄다.
form.why: The ㅡ of 끄 drops before -어: 끄 + 었어요 → 껐어요.

ko_meaning: 닫혀 있는 문이나 창문을 움직여서 안이 보이게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To move a closed door or window so the inside is open

example.en: It was hot, so I opened the window.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 열다 before 수 있어요 ('can open').
form.why: A ㄹ-stem just keeps its ㄹ: 열 + ㄹ 수 있다 → 열 수 있다 (not 열을).

ko_meaning_en: To shut something that is open

example.en: The wind was blowing, so I closed the window.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 닫다.
form.why: 닫다 is regular (not like 듣다 → 들어요), and 닫 has ㅏ: 닫 + 았어요 → 닫았어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from outside to inside

example.en: My younger sibling got angry and went into their room.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 들어가다.
form.why: 가 + 았어요 → 갔어요 (the two ㅏ merge), so 들어가다 → 들어갔어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from inside to outside

example.ko: 비가 와서 밖에 나갈 수 없어요.
example.roman: Biga waseo bakke nagal su eopseoyo.
example.en: It's raining, so I can't go outside.

form.q_en: Pick the form of 나가다 before 수 없어요 ('can't go out').
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 없다: after a vowel stem add ㄹ, so 나가 + ㄹ → 나갈 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: To come from outside to inside

example.en: It's cold outside, so come in quickly.

form.q_en: Pick the 'because' form that can come before a request.
form.why: Before a request like -(으)세요, use -(으)니까 for 'because'. -아서/어서 cannot come before a request.

ko_meaning_en: To come from inside to outside

example.en: The movie ended and I came out of the theater.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'out of (a place)'.
form.why: With 나오다, 에서 marks the place you come out of. 에 would mark the place you come to.

ko_meaning: 좋아해서 시간이 있을 때 자주 하는 일
ko_meaning_en: Something you like and often do when you have time

example.en: I want to meet friends who have the same hobby.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 같다 ('the same').
form.why: 같다 is an adjective, so the present modifier is -은: 같 + 은 → 같은. -는 is for verbs.

ko_meaning_en: Going up a mountain

example.en: I bought new shoes to go hiking.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'in order to go'.
form.why: -(으)려고 means 'in order to' and works with any main verb. -(으)러 only works when the main verb is 가다/오다.

ko_meaning: 물에서 팔과 다리를 움직여 앞으로 가는 운동
ko_meaning_en: Exercise of moving through water with your arms and legs

example.en: I want to learn to swim, but I don't have time.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.why: -지만 shows contrast ('but'). -어서 and -(으)니까 mean 'because', and -(으)면 means 'if'.

ko_meaning_en: Catching fish

example.en: I went fishing with my dad on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that shows the purpose of going.
form.why: -(으)러 + 가다 means 'go in order to do': 낚시하러 갔어요 = went fishing.

ko_meaning_en: Something fun you play on a computer or phone

example.ko: 동생은 게임을 하면 밥도 안 먹어요.
example.roman: Dongsaeng-eun geimeul hamyeon bapdo an meogeoyo.
example.en: When my younger brother plays games, he doesn't even eat.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the particle that means 'even'.
form.ko: 동생은 게임을 하면 밥___ 안 먹어요.
form.why: 도 means 'also / even': 밥도 안 먹어요 = doesn't even eat. 먹다 needs an object, so 밥이 is wrong.

ko_meaning: 발로 공을 차서 골에 넣는 운동
ko_meaning_en: A sport where you kick a ball into a goal

example.en: My son is good at soccer, so he's famous at school.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 잘하다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: 하다 verbs become 해서: 잘하 + 여서 → 잘해서. -아서/어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: A sport where you hit a ball with a bat and run

example.en: I'm going to watch baseball this evening.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 보다.
form.why: After a vowel stem, add ㄹ: 보 + ㄹ → 볼 거예요 = will watch.

ko_meaning: 공을 손으로 던져서 높은 바구니에 넣는 운동
ko_meaning_en: A sport where you throw a ball by hand into a high basket

example.en: He's tall, so he's good at basketball.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 크다 + -어서.
form.why: The ㅡ of 크 drops before -어: 크 + 어서 → 커서. -어서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 그물을 사이에 두고 라켓으로 공을 치는 운동
ko_meaning_en: A sport where you hit a ball over a net with a racket

example.en: My older sister plays tennis every morning.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the verb Koreans use with 테니스.
form.why: You 'hit' tennis: 테니스를 치다 → 쳐요. 타다 is for rides, 부르다 for songs and 신다 for shoes.

ko_meaning_en: A Korean martial art that uses the hands and feet

example.en: My daughter is planning to learn taekwondo.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the ending for 'plan to' (-(으)려고 하다).
form.why: 배우 ends in a vowel, so add -려고: 배우려고 해요 = plans to learn. -으려고 is for consonant stems.

ko_meaning_en: To make a picture with a pencil or brush

example.en: The child drew Mom's face.

tokens.note: a noun before a noun can mean 'of'

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 그리다.
form.why: 그리 + 었어요 → 그렸어요 (ㅣ + ㅓ join into ㅕ).

ko_meaning_en: To move your body to music

example.en: I danced with my friends at the party.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 춤추다.
form.why: 추 + 었어요 → 췄어요 (ㅜ + ㅓ join into ㅝ).

ko_meaning: 손이나 물건으로 세게 때리다; 피아노나 테니스 같은 것을 하다
ko_meaning_en: To strike hard; to play the piano, tennis and so on

example.en: If I play the guitar in the evening, my neighbors don't like it.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 치다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 치 ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 치면.

ko_meaning_en: To walk slowly while relaxing

example.en: After dinner, I took a walk in the park.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 먹다 + -고 ('ate and then').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem: 먹 + 고 → 먹고.

ko_meaning: 재미있는 것이나 새로운 곳을 보며 다니다
ko_meaning_en: To go around looking at interesting things or new places

example.en: When I go to Seoul, I want to look around the museums.

form.q_en: Pick the form that goes with 싶어요 ('want to').
form.why: 'Want to' is -고 싶다: 구경하고 싶어요. The other endings cannot go before 싶다.

ko_meaning_en: To have nothing to do, so nothing is fun

example.en: I had nothing to do on the weekend, so I was bored.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 없다 + -어서.
form.why: 없 has ㅓ, so it takes -어서: 없어서 (said [업써서]).

en: to be scary; to be afraid
ko_meaning: 어떤 것 때문에 마음이 놀라고 불안하다
ko_meaning_en: To feel startled and uneasy because of something

example.en: Walking alone at night is scary.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 걷다 + -(으)면.
form.why: 걷다 is ㄷ-irregular: ㄷ becomes ㄹ before a vowel, so 걷 + 으면 → 걸으면. 걸면 comes from 걸다 'to hang'.

ko_meaning_en: To feel sad because no one is with you

example.en: I live alone abroad, so I'm lonely.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 살다 + -아서 ('live, so').
form.why: 살 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 살아서. ㄹ stays because the ending starts with a vowel.

ko_meaning: 나쁜 일이 생길 것 같아서 마음이 편하지 않다
ko_meaning_en: To feel uneasy because something bad might happen

example.en: My mom will worry, so I have to go home early.

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'have to go in (home)'.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 means 'have to': 들어가 + 아야 → 들어가야 해요.

en: to be enjoyable; to be fun
ko_meaning_en: To feel good and have fun

example.en: Have a nice weekend!

tokens.note: ㅂ irregular modifier: 즐겁 + 은 → 즐거운

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 즐겁다.
form.why: 즐겁다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before -은, so 즐겁 + 은 → 즐거운.

en: to be surprised; to be startled
ko_meaning: 생각하지 못한 일 때문에 갑자기 마음이 크게 움직이다
ko_meaning_en: To be suddenly shaken by something you didn't expect

example.en: A cat suddenly came out, and I was startled.

form.q_en: Pick the correct past form of 놀라다.
form.why: 놀라 + 았어요 → 놀랐어요. 놀랬어요 is a common spelling mistake.

ko_meaning_en: To shed tears because you are sad or hurt

example.en: The baby is crying because it's hungry.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 배고프다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: The ㅡ of 프 drops, and the vowel before it (고) has ㅗ, so it takes -아서: 배고파서.

ko_meaning: 기쁘거나 재미있어서 얼굴이 밝아지거나 소리를 내다
ko_meaning_en: To brighten your face or make a sound because you are happy or amused

example.en: I heard my friend's story and laughed a lot.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 듣다 + -고.
form.why: 듣다 keeps ㄷ before a consonant: 듣고. It changes to ㄹ only before a vowel (들어요). 들고 comes from 들다 'to hold'.

ko_meaning: 어떤 사람이나 것을 아주 좋아하고 아끼다
ko_meaning_en: To like and care about someone or something very much

example.en: Dad really loves Mom.

tokens.note: 를 marks the object after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the person who is loved.
form.why: 사랑하다 takes an object, so 엄마 needs 를 (after a vowel). 가 marks a subject, and 은 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: To not like

example.en: Cats hate water.

form.q_en: Pick the form that fits after 물을 (an object).
form.why: 싫어하다 is a verb and takes an object with 을/를. 싫다 is an adjective and needs 이/가 (물이 싫어요).

ko_meaning_en: The whole of a person or animal, from head to foot

example.ko: 몸이 안 좋아서 회사에 못 갔어요.
example.roman: Momi an joaseo hoesae mot gasseoyo.
example.en: I wasn't feeling well, so I couldn't go to work.

tokens.note: 몸이 안 좋다 = to feel unwell

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'so, because'.
form.why: -아서 gives the reason: 안 좋아서 = because I wasn't well. -(으)면 means 'if', and 좋을 cannot link two clauses.

ko_meaning_en: The part between the head and the body

example.en: I caught a cold, so my throat hurts.

tokens.note: 감기에 걸리다 = to catch a cold
이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 아프다.
form.why: The ㅡ of 프 drops, and 아 has ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 아파요.

ko_meaning: 목 아래 양쪽 옆에 있는 부분
ko_meaning_en: The part on each side below the neck

example.en: My older brother is tall and has broad shoulders.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 크다 + -고 ('tall and').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem with no change: 크 + 고 → 크고.

ko_meaning_en: The middle part of the body, behind the stomach

example.en: My lower back hurts, so I'm going to go to the hospital.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the form for 'plan to go' (-(으)려고 하다).
form.why: -(으)려고 하다 means 'plan to': 가려고 해요. -(으)러 needs 가다/오다 right after it, not 하다.

ko_meaning_en: The part in the middle of the leg that bends

example.en: I fell down and hurt my knee.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 무릎.
form.why: 무릎 ends in a consonant (ㅍ), so the object particle is 을. 를 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 목이 아플 때 '콜록' 하고 나오는 소리
ko_meaning_en: The 'cough cough' sound that comes out when your throat hurts

example.en: I kept coughing, so I took some medicine.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 나다 + -아서.
form.why: 나 + 아서 → 나서 (the two ㅏ merge). -아서 never takes the past tense.

ko_meaning: 감기에 걸렸을 때 코에서 나오는 물
ko_meaning_en: Liquid that comes out of your nose when you have a cold

example.en: If you have a runny nose, take this medicine.

tokens.note: 콧물이 나다 = to have a runny nose
드시다 = polite word for 먹다; -(으)세요 = request

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'if'.
form.why: -(으)면 means 'if'. -아서 cannot come before a request like -(으)세요, and -지만 means 'but'.

ko_meaning_en: Pain in the head

example.en: If you have a headache, you should rest.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct 'have to' form of 쉬다.
form.why: 쉬 has ㅟ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -어야: 쉬어야 해요.

ko_meaning_en: To get injured somewhere on your body

example.en: The hand I hurt yesterday still hurts.

tokens.note: past noun modifier: 다치 + ㄴ → 다친

form.q_en: Pick the modifier for 'that I hurt yesterday' (past).
form.why: For a past action, a verb takes -(으)ㄴ before a noun: 다치 + ㄴ → 다친. -는 is present, -(으)ㄹ is future.

ko_meaning_en: For a sick body to become healthy again

example.en: If you take the medicine, you'll get better soon.

form.q_en: Pick the correct future form of 낫다.
form.why: 낫다 is ㅅ-irregular: ㅅ drops before a vowel, so 낫 + 을 → 나을 거예요.

ko_meaning: 사람이 똑바로 섰을 때 발부터 머리까지의 길이
ko_meaning_en: The length from your feet to your head when you stand straight

example.en: Basketball players are really tall.

tokens.note: 들 = plural, 은 marks the topic

form.q_en: Pick the adjective Koreans use with 키 ('tall').
form.why: Height (키) goes with 크다/작다: 키가 커요 = is tall. 높다 is for buildings and mountains.

en: to be fat; to be chubby
ko_meaning_en: To have a lot of fat, so the body is wide

example.ko: 우리 개는 너무 많이 먹어서 뚱뚱해요.
example.roman: Uri gaeneun neomu mani meogeoseo ttungttunghaeyo.
example.en: Our dog eats too much, so it's fat.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 먹다 + -어서.
form.why: 먹 has ㅓ, so it takes -어서: 먹어서 (said [머거서]).

ko_meaning_en: To have a thin, nice-looking body

example.en: My older sister eats a lot, but she's slim.

form.q_en: Pick the connector meaning 'but'.
form.why: -지만 shows contrast: she eats a lot, but she's slim. -어서 and -(으)니까 mean 'because'.

en: to be good-looking; to be handsome
ko_meaning_en: To have a handsome, nice-looking face

example.en: That actor is really handsome.

tokens.note: looks are usually said with the past form

form.q_en: Koreans describe looks with the past form. Pick it.
form.why: 잘생기 + 었어요 → 잘생겼어요 (ㅣ + ㅓ → ㅕ). It means 'is good-looking' now.

ko_meaning_en: Small and pretty, so lovable

example.en: The little puppy is so cute.

form.q_en: Pick the correct present form of 귀엽다.
form.why: 귀엽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 귀엽 + 어요 → 귀여워요.

en: to be clear (sky); to be clean (water)
ko_meaning_en: To have no clouds and nice weather

example.ko: 오늘은 하늘이 맑아서 산이 잘 보여요.
example.roman: Oneureun haneuri malgaseo sani jal boyeoyo.
example.en: The sky is clear today, so I can see the mountains well.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 맑다 + -아서.
form.why: 맑 has ㅏ, so it takes -아서: 맑아서. It sounds like [말가서] but is spelled 맑아서.

ko_meaning_en: So many clouds that the sky is dark

example.en: Tomorrow it will be cloudy and rainy.

form.q_en: Pick the future form of 오다 ('will come').
form.why: After a vowel stem, add ㄹ: 오 + ㄹ → 올 거예요. 온 is a past modifier and does not fit 내일.

ko_meaning: 하늘에 떠 있는 하얗거나 회색인 것
ko_meaning_en: The white or gray things floating in the sky

example.en: There isn't a single cloud in the sky.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant
하나도 + negative = not a single one

form.q_en: Pick the phrase meaning 'not a single one' (with 없어요).
form.why: 하나도 + a negative means 'not even one'. 한 needs a counter, and 일 is not used this way.

ko_meaning_en: For the wind to move

example.en: It's very windy, so wear a hat.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 불다 + -(으)니까.
form.why: For a ㄹ-stem, ㄹ drops before ㄴ and no 으 is added: 불 + 니까 → 부니까.

ko_meaning: 비가 올 때 머리 위에 쓰는 물건
ko_meaning_en: Something you hold over your head when it rains

example.en: I left my umbrella on the subway when I got off.

tokens.note: 에 marks where something is put
을 marks the object after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 놓다 + -고.
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem: 놓 + 고 → 놓고. It sounds like [노코] but is spelled 놓고.

ko_meaning_en: To have nothing dirty on it

example.en: The hotel room was spacious and clean, so it was nice.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 깨끗하다 + -아서/어서.
form.why: 하다 words take -여서, which becomes 해서: 깨끗해서.

ko_meaning_en: Not clean because dust or dirt is on it

example.en: Put dirty clothes in the washing machine.

tokens.note: ㅂ irregular modifier: 더럽 + 은 → 더러운

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 더럽다.
form.why: 더럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before -은, so 더럽 + 은 → 더러운.

ko_meaning_en: Having no sound, or only a little

example.en: I want to study at a quiet cafe.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the modifier form of 조용하다 ('quiet').
form.why: 조용하다 is an adjective, so the present modifier is -ㄴ: 조용한. -는 is only for verbs.

en: to be noisy; to be loud
ko_meaning_en: Sounds are too loud and too many

example.en: It's noisy outside, so please close the window.

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 시끄럽다 + -(으)니까.
form.why: 시끄럽다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ + 으 becomes 우, so 시끄럽 + 으니까 → 시끄러우니까.

en: to be comfortable; to be convenient
ko_meaning_en: Your body or mind feels at ease, not strained

example.en: These shoes are light and comfortable.

tokens.note: -고 = and; ㅂ stays before a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the correct form of 가볍다 + -고 ('light and').
form.why: -고 goes straight on the stem: 가볍 + 고 → 가볍고. The ㅂ only changes before a vowel.
